facts: The scoring by ONTOSCORE is on the basis of an ontology.
The authors apply ONTOSCORE to the task of scoring alternative speech recognition hypotheses.
The alternative speech recognition hypotheses are scored in terms of their semantic coherence.
The authors conducted an annotation experiment.
The annotation experiment showed that human annotators can reliably differentiate between semantically coherent and incoherent speech recognition hypotheses.
An evaluation of ONTOSCORE against the annotated data was performed.
ONTOSCORE successfully classifies 73.2% in a German corpus of 2.284 SRHs as either coherent or incoherent.
The corpus used for evaluation is a German corpus.
The classification by ONTOSCORE is as either coherent or incoherent.
The baseline for the evaluation is 54.55%.
SRH stands for speech recognition hypotheses.
